utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. If there is nothing else that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this Bench, we will continue with the direct examination by the Prosecution. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, we will now begin to discuss some of the issues in your narrative as they relate to the Zvornik Brigade area. I believe we are in the chronology of about 13 July, and what is the first exhibit that brings us to this area?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can refer back to Prosecution Exhibit 208, which we saw yesterday. Just a refresher on the quick discussion between Colonel Milanovic, a Drina Corps officer and the Palma duty officer with respect to inquiring as to the availability of a bulldozer with a scoop, a bucket loader, in fact, and being told that there are not any available at this time. This is the first instance that I see where in a document or in an intercept we can start to see the shifting of criminal activity or the involvement of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade in the actual manifestations of potential criminal activity. The next document is Prosecution Exhibit P510. This is a vehicle work log for one particular vehicle in the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. In this case an Opel Rekord registration number P-4528. By way of some background, each vehicle in the Zvornik Infantry Brigade and, in fact, each vehicle in all of the units of the VRS was required under regulations to maintain a log which was updated on a daily basis which contained elements of information concerning the mileage driven, the fuel used, and other routine maintenance or other issues that were necessary to record pursuant to the daily functioning of the vehicle. This particular vehicle registration number P-4528, operated under the control during July 1995 of the assistant commander for security of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. And the three individuals listed here Milorad Bircakovic, Mirko Ristic, and Misko Arapovic are members of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade military police company.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As part of the documents that we have seized from the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, we have seized unit rosters for the July 1995 time frame, and the names of these individuals are members of the military police on that log. If I can turn to the second page in the English language translation, and perhaps before I do, it may be instructive. This is what the actual logbook looks like in B/C/S. And if you will go to -- one of the pages is missing. I just want to note out that it does, in fact, have the names of Mirko Ristic and Misko Arapovic. Going to the second page of this document, I would highlight for the attention of the Court the notations with respect to 13 July 1995, noting the trips that the vehicle made during the course of that day. Standard is what is normally put in there to refer to the garrison of the Zvornik Brigade, which was the former Standard shoe factory. IKM, of course, is the forward command post, Zvornik local. Then you will see trips listed to Orahovac, Zvornik, Orahovac, back to Standard, down to Bratunac, and then a return to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, I notice there's no times listed. So from this log, is there any way to determine at what time of day these trips were made?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, there is not. I would, however, note that what we are able to determine is the number of people in the vehicle generally, which is listed as 3 and total number of kilometres travelled in this respect, which is 209 on that day. Moving to the 14th of July on the second page or the third page of the English language translation, where it notes, first working for 7469, VP 7469 is the military postal code number for the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. It also reflects trips back and forth between Standard, Orahovac, Divic. It also lists now trips to the location of Rocevic 164 kilometres that day. And then continuing on the 15th of July, Karakaj, Rocevic. Another trip to Rocevic, Kuzluk. On the 16th, includes trips to Kula, which we know is the school in Pilica. Pilica proper. Local, which we interpret to be the local Zvornik area Standard, Kuzluk, Rocevic. On the 17th the vehicle goes down to Kravica and then back to the Zvornik area. So as you can tell, the pattern of travel for this particular vehicle from the 13th to the 17th, many of the locations that this vehicle stops at are, in fact, known holding sites for Bosnian Muslim men in schools in the Zvornik Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, let me ask you just about one of those sites, Orahovac. Now, Orahovac -- we've heard about Orahovac on the 13th -- excuse me, the 14th of July where prisoners were held and executed. Do you know if there was any military purpose for that school prior to -- prior to the 14th or after the 14th of July. Just give us a little bit of background on Orahovac, that school?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one point in time in late 1992, the school was actually used as a headquarters for the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. But in July 1995, to the best of my knowledge in researching the documents and other information, that school had no potential use or no active military use from the beginning of July until approximately 16 or 17 July. On or about the 17th of July when the unit of the 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade departed the Bratunac area and was reassigned back to the Zvornik Brigade area, that battalion was garrisoned at that school in Orahovac. But during the first month of -- the first couple of weeks of July, there was no significant military purpose for that school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I -- just a point of clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Earlier, and I failed to jump up fast enough, when the gentleman was talking about July 13th, he had indicated that there were 209 miles, I believe, or kilometres, but there seems to be -- and he made references to the Orahovac on that instance. But there doesn't seem to be anything on that line and I guess I want some clarification, because we have two July 13ths, one designating 209 kilometres, but the one dealing with Orahovac doesn't have anything. So if he could clarify that for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Since this question is related to the clarification, I think this intervention is up to the point. Mr. McCloskey, could you ask some questions to this witness so that we could have a clearer picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, Mr. Karnavas -- you see what he's pointing out?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the B/C/S original of that particular log sheet. If you'll notice the last two lines, you can see where the number of trips travelled -- they clearly combine both of the lines, and the writing is actually going right through the line, indicating that it's covering both of those columns. For clarity in the English language translation, the translator has just placed it on one line, but I think it's clear from the B/C/S that what we're talking about is the combined trips of those two columns or those two rows.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And what is the next exhibit in this area?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next exhibit is Prosecution Exhibit 509, which is the operations duty log of the forward command post of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, which was established at Kitovnice. And in this particular document on page 6 of the English language translation, the notation on 13 July by Major Galic of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, that he took over duty unscheduled from Lieutenant Drago Nikolic at 2300 hours that evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And why do you find that significant?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect in time by approximately 2300 hours on 13 July 1995, buses were already -- the first convoys of buses carrying Bosnian Muslim men were already en route from Bratunac towards the school in Orahovac. And according to survivor statements and other military police documents which we have, the military police and the buses started arriving at the school approximately midnight or shortly thereafter. In this particular instance, Drago Nikolic being relieved of his responsibility at the IKM to oversee this process is a natural course of events. And as I've always noted, this is an exchange that could only take place with the approval of the brigade, at that time, deputy commander. This is not something that these two officers in and of themselves could have effected without approval of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And has the testimony of Mr. Obrenovic confirmed your initial analysis on that point?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, in that respect it's consistent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you mentioned other military police documents relating the military police to Orahovac. What were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them in specific we'll get to in a future exhibit, which is the July 1995 roster of the military police company of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, which shows where locations of each military police person are on a given day. And there will be some notations on that which will indicate military police being present at Orahovac on the 14th. There is another document which is part of my narrative report, which is from the rear services branch, noting that approximately midnight on the 13th of July, a truck was dispatched to Orahovac to provide food and water for the military police who were present at -- who were present and arriving at the school. So it's putting all of these together is where I make my assessment that approximately midnight the first contingent of military police arrived at the school in Orahovac where they would begin guarding the prisoners, and the prisoners started arriving shortly thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next document is Prosecution Exhibit 511, and it is the first page of the military police roster for July of 1995. And it's a somewhat difficult document between the English and B/C/S translation, and for clarity sake, this is what the actual B/C/S version of the document page 1 looks like. And our translators just did not put in the numbers because they are evident in Latin text. And of course on this side, notes July of 1995. In this particular respect, it is a handwritten listing of the individuals assigned to the military police. And notations as to where everyone is on given days. If I can go back to the English language translation version in this particular case. This will be the first page. What this document indicates in the original B/C/S version that I have to note was altered before it became -- before it came into the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor is that a number, and I believe the exact number is 14, of military police officers were at the school at Orahovac on 14 July 1995. And this will include the commander of the military police company, Captain Miomir Jasikovac. On the back of the B/C/S sheet, there will be a legend in B/C/S which identifies the following symbols. I'll find one more here. On the B/C/S version of this document, you have it here. What you will be unable to see on the Xerox copies but is evident on the original as well as in the Dutch laboratory reports on the document is that legend notations O for Orahovac and R for Rocevic have been erased.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Does it actually say R for Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe does, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we did not bring that original today. We can bring it to you. I was not -- I don't believe that is really a contested issue, but we can provide you the original, and there is an expert report that points out what Mr. Butler is saying as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler can you describe -- can you go back to the original log and explain to the Court how you believe this altering was done and on what dates.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the day listing for 14 July for the military police officers, and they are listed by name and by narrative, what will happen is that the notations, the original handwritten notations for O will have been erased and a T indicating that the troops are actually out on the terrain will have been replacing it. And on the 15th, you will have similar notations and erasure marks for, I believe, a lesser number of military police at Rocevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. I'm not sure whether the Prosecutor will be paying attention to this exhibit P109. It is the book of the duty operations officer at the forward command post. And since I see that we are moving forward, I would kindly ask, now that we have the opportunity, to raise this issue of the authenticity of this document, it's provenance. How did the Prosecution get it in the first place in order to have a basis for the answers that were already provided by the witness concerning the contents for the 13th at the forward command post. So where does this document come from? If we settle that, I will not be coming back to this issue anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey. Please lay some foundations by asking some questions to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we can go back to the forward command post logbook that you've referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And for Your Honours' knowledge, we have an index of all Mr. Butler's exhibits and where they came from that we'll be providing and, of course, have been provided to the Defence. But I can certainly in -- especially on documents the Defence is concerned about have Mr. Butler talk about that, as I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, where did this, to your knowledge, logbook, the forward command post logbook, come from?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular document was obtained by the Office of the Prosecutor during its search of the headquarters of the former Zvornik Brigade in early 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And have you had a chance to review the original document for the analysis you've been speaking of?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And if we could go on to the next in the series.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 512, which I only highlight before the Court as the report of the Dutch forensic laboratory with respect to the erasure markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did you use this and study this report in your overall analysis?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did, with respect to the erasure markings. Again, however, I would note that I've also reviewed the original document and the erasure markings are fairly evident by the naked eye. They don't require a whole lot of work to see those.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And to clarify, Mr. Butler, on the report regarding R, I don't see any specific reference to Rocevic. Could you be mistaken on that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will have to check back. If I'm mistaken, then I will apologise for that. Yes, sir, I apologise for that. I am, in fact, mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you this wouldn't be the last mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, we'll identify them as we go. And what is the next document you want to discuss?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Continuing on with the company logs, I would like to discuss document -- the Prosecution Exhibit 514, which is the -- in English, this is the second page of it, but this is the log of the engineering company of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade for 1995. In this particular document, I would raise to the Court's attention in the 3rd Platoon, there will be a number of individuals and their duties will be listed as RGM. Those individuals are, in fact, heavy equipment operators, and we will see their names listed on the logs or vehicle logs of pieces of earth-moving equipment that are subsequently involved in the burial of bodies after mass executions. Turning to Prosecution Exhibit 515, this is the vehicle log for a backhoe excavator, registration number C-3117 for the period 1 through 31 July 1995. The two individuals noted on it are also on the engineer company list as heavy equipment operators. This particular document reflects that on 14 July 1995, working for the VRS, the machine travelled from Base, which is in this context is the base of the engineer company Orahovac, and returned. It notes the activity trench digging, and notes that this operation took six hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Are you aware from your study of the materials any engineering work taking place in and around Orahovac, aside from the grave digging that survivors talked about?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. The only activity that I'm aware of is the grave digging activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, could we go to Exhibit 513. I know I may have gotten you a little off the -- our order, but can you describe -- and we're going to need to come up a little bit, what this is the English translation of. Could we come out so the ELMO can see that completely. Mr. ELMO.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: While that's occurring, this document is an extract from the engineer company commander's logbook or orders book which runs through the period of July 1995. This orders book was also seized by the Office of the Prosecutor in the search of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade in early 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe your knowledge to what this function of this book was.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The function of this book is that in the morning of every day, the commander or its representative would list the daily tasks of the unit. And as you compare the tasks listed here from 1 through 5 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. Maybe it's interpretation. I see "commander" in the transcript, and in fact the differences between commander and commanding officer, since this is pivoting around the commander of the company, I would like the witness when he says "commander," to specify whose commander or whose commanding officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we can clarify that. He's talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, who are you talking about when you're talking about the engineering company?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular instance, the engineering company commander is Dragan Jevtic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And before you were interrupted, you were discussing briefly the function of this book.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I had indicated, in this particular case the daily orders of the unit were placed down. And it indicated what tasks the unit would be involved in through the course of the day. It also reported some of the more administrative manners with respect to guard duty at the explosive depot and who the duty officer of the company was and whether days off could be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I notice number 3 on task is to set an ambush with combat group, on the order of the brigade chief of staff. Can you briefly tell us what you think that is.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we refer back to testimony that's before the Court as well as documents that are in my narrative, as the context of the history indicates, by the evening of 12 July 1995, and through the day of the 13th of July, 1995, a group of individuals from the engineer company led by their commander were assembled and were taken into the field by then-Major Obrenovic as part of other forces that were to block and ambush the Muslim column. And I believe that item 3 reflects that activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And the original of this particular document, do you have that with you. Do you know at the bottom, is there a signature for the commander?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, there is. And unfortunately it's covered by the exhibit sticker on this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And can you -- in that -- the signature, that has been acknowledged to be the signature of Dragan Jevtic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. However, it should be noted that as we inquired on that, given Mr. Jevtic's presence in the field during this period, it was his indication that these documents or this book, that he signed it for the blank pages of it after he had returned from the operation. So there is no instance in this particular case where the commander came back from the field every day to sign the morning orders book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, this is for 14 July. You have just gone over a logbook for an excavator working at Orahovac on the 14th of July. I don't see any tasks here for the 14th July. How can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. What that indicates to me is that the orders to the engineering company to have earth-moving equipment go to Orahovac were received after the notations in this book were laid out for the day, which would mean sometime in the late morning, early afternoon, the engineer company received these orders, not in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next document.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is Prosecution Exhibit 516. And this is the vehicle work log of what is a vehicle known as a Torpedo Excavator. On the top, it highlights the notation Birac Holding, which indicates to me that this was a piece of equipment normally associated with that particular civilian engineering company and was requisitioned during some part of this month and certainly these days for use by the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how -- what do you know, if anything, about that requisitioning process?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally, given the fact that it is engineering equipment in this particular case, that requisitioning process normally would take place first through the principal staff officer, which in this particular instance would be Major Jokic, the chief of engineering services of the Zvornik Brigade, it would also go through Captain Sreten Milosevic, who is the chief of rear services, and then the request would be made through the Ministry of Defence office in Zvornik for the particular piece of equipment. That is the formalised process that should have taken place. I don't know whether that process may have been streamlined as a result of the activities that were occurring.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know actually when that process for this machine took place? Could it have taken place in June or July before the Srebrenica mess?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't. Again while the vehicle work log notes that it's valid from 1 to 31 July, 1995, the first notation for fuel for the month of July is listed as 11 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, the -- are there any indications -- who are these -- can we tell from this form who Ristanovic and Milos Mitrovic are?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both those individuals are identified, going back to the engineer company roster. From the 3rd Platoon, the Heavy Equipment Platoon, number 9, Ristanovic. And on the second grouping, number 8, Milos Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that RGM --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Construction machine operator. There is on this particular page, which is page 6 of the English language translation, in very small writing there will be a footnote indicating the English language translation of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is that a reflection of the actual original document or an interpreter's interpretation of what that means?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the original document. It says RGM, but of course there's nothing on the bottom, which would indicate that that would be an interpreter's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Going back down to 516, the second page indicating usage of the vehicle notes that on 11 July 1995 the vehicle was engaged for four hours digging up cherry trees at the military farm. It notes on 14 July 1995 it was engaged for five hours digging trenches in Orahovac. And there are subsequent notations on the 16th of July indicating digging trenches in Kozluk, which we will get to later in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why don't you just, while we've got this document up there, tell us what you think these Kozluk notations mean.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The notations for Kozluk are associated with the burial of bodies at the location of the former bottle factory and Kozluk, and I believe the investigation has determined that the Bosnian Muslims from the school in Rocevic were buried at that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go on to the next exhibit. I believe it is 517.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the vehicle work log for a TAM 75 truck, registration number M-5264. And this particular vehicle, according to other vehicle records that we have, is working for the engineering company of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade at that time and is assigned to that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know a TAM 75?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, the TAM 75 is a medium capacity cargo truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what do you make of this vehicle log and this TAM?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The driver is a member of the engineering company and he's listed on that log sheet. And in this particular instance, highlighting the activities of this truck for 14, 15, 16 and 17 July 1995, indicating that on the 14th of July multiple trips between the base, the engineering company headquarters and Orahovac. On the 15th of July, similar trips and in one handwritten notation it says, "Three times between Base and Orahovac." And during this period of time from late afternoon on the 14th until approximately 2300 hours on the 14th, the engineer equipment company is working. The equipment is working digging graves sites and then work resumes at first light on the morning of the 15th. Continuing on to the 16th, you see trips between Kuzluk, Orahovac, back and forth to Kuzluk and Orahovac. Again reflecting movement of engineer equipment from Orahovac to the grave sites or the sites where they're digging graves in Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, it seems to me that there's some problems with the LiveNote, but now it's okay. But anyway, that paragraph will be made out after the session. Since the LiveNote is okay, you may move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. I did not see that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Butler, if you can continue just to describe the daily activity of this truck and your knowledge briefly related to each day that is going on.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we look at this instance on 17 July notes trips back and forth between Kula and Base. Now, as I've previously indicated in my testimony, Orahovac, Kozluk are -- in the case of Orahovac, it's both an execution and a burial site. Kozluk is a known burial site. And Kula is a -- the school in Pilica, which is also a known holding site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And an engineering vehicle -- let's go on to the next document. I believe it's 518. What is this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is an extract of a fuel dispersal logbook that the OTP seized during its search of the former headquarters of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. For further clarification, this is the B/C/S front cover of that book. On the 14th of July, it reflects that 200 litres of D2 diesel fuel was dispersed to the engineering which corresponds with their use of the equipment on the 14th of July 1995. I would also highlight for the future, in notation 685 on 17 July, you will see a notation for 100 litres of D2 for a BGH-700. That is another piece of earth-moving equipment that we will see associated with burial activity at the Branjevo Military Farm on 17 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. What is the next document you've chosen?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next document, staying with the theme of the events that are occurring on 14 July 1995, is Prosecution Exhibit 227, which is an intercept between General Zivanovic and Major Jokic that occurs at 0910 hours on 14 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, who do you think Major Jokic is in this context of this conversation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On 14 July 1995, Major Jokic is functioning as the duty officer of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. He is the duty operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And is that mentioned anywhere in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular conversation, not only does Major Jokic compromise his own identity, it's what we call in the business a voice compromise. He also compromises his duty position that day, as a duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And where is that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it is approximately half way down the page. You see the notation "J: Here from, as a duty officer."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, 14 July you have -- you testified earlier that General Zivanovic was no longer the commander. How do you explain General Zivanovic being in a conversation with Major Jokic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular instance, we know that General Zivanovic remained in the Vlasenica command post. As indicated in the -- we had always suspected -- let me bring a little history into that. This has always been a rather large issue with respect to the issue of General Zivanovic and when he relinquished command of the corps. In reviewing this issue and in doing the associated analysis, there were some indications that on 14 July 1995, that there were some communication difficulties between the established Drina Corps forward command post in Krivace and the rest of the brigade. And at the time I indicated that that may be some possible reason why they're calling the Vlasenica headquarters. It may also very well be that Major Jokic is calling his superior duty officer, which on 14 July would be Colonel Predrag Jokic [sic] at the Drina Corps, and in fact is placed in the conversation also with General Zivanovic to brief him of the situation. The last piece of information which was recently received on that came in concert with the 14 July daily combat report of the Drina Corps, which did indicate that they were having communications difficulties between the Vlasenica headquarters and the IKM in Pribicevac. So in this particular case --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The IKM in Pribicevac?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The IKM in Krivace, which was for Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Our pronunciation may not clearly identify for the Court what we're talking about. Do you see that on the map, the forward command post for the Zepa Operation

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I'll point that out on the map -- for the Zepa Operation -- this was the forward command post for the Srebrenica Operation, which was Pribicevac. For the Zepa Operation, the Drina Corps established a forward command post in Krivace.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Again that's the 16.1 exhibit that Mr. Butler's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honour. Just one more thing in the transcript that could be a problem, that's what we've been discussing for a long time since last week. The expert said a second ago that a conversation took place between duty officer Palma and duty officer Predrag Jokic at the Drina Corps. Is that a mistake? Could it be Predrag Jocic, with a C instead of a K. I think we should clarify this now to avoid further misunderstanding, because it seems to me that the duty officer on Zlatar at that time was Predrag Jokic or maybe Jocic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think your intervention is about a clarification. Let's make that clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Butler, could you -- do you understand what Mr. Stojanovic means?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And if I could have a second. I will make apologies in advance because I think we're all a victim of my poor pronunciation of names. I believe there is a document here which, if I can just show in advance -- assuming I do have this one, but it is the individual in question is a Colonel Predrag -- it's Jocic, J-o-c-i-c. I do believe I may have a document which shows his name listed. If not, I can get one at the break to make it perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there would be no problem, because that is precisely what we are saying. The man's name was Jocic, and that was precisely why we were asking those questions of people who did the intercepts. And it could have been a problem if it had remained Jokic in the transcript. I think we've clarified it now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, in this exhibit, 227, is there any indication that Predrag Jocic was involved in this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. And like I said, understanding with respect to the intercept that over sometimes poor-quality lines the name would be garbled. That's why I value instances where not only will one of the subscribers compromise himself by just a name, he will also compromise himself by his rank or other identifying features. So in that respect, as much as possible, I try to take those into effect when offer up my analysis of whom I think conversations are occurring between and what they potentially mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Getting back, I think, to my original question about General Zivanovic, what was he -- to your knowledge, what was he doing in the Vlasenica headquarters on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, General Zivanovic was packing up his personal effects to leave the headquarters. Certainly while he would no longer be the corps commander, as a general and the former corps commander, he would just not the taken himself out of what, as it turns out to be, a developing significant military situation just by virtue of not being the commander. And in this particular instance, he does and first take the report of Major Jokic, wants to know where he's receiving his information from. And in the second page indicates that Mane needs to be informed. And in this respect, Mane is Mane Djuric, the deputy head of the Zvornik CSB. And that is clarified in the next statement from General Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Jokic also says, "The chief of staff Obrenovic is coming now, so we'll take some steps immediately." What do you take that to mean?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the context of this conversation on 14 July 1995 at 0910 hours in the morning, I take that as an indication that Major Jokic believes that Major Obrenovic is in-bound from his location in the field, and those steps will be taken, that he will inform him as soon as he arrives.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In-bound where?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In-bound from his field location to the headquarters of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: From the intercepts or any documents that you have reviewed in this case, have you been able to find any indications that Major Obrenovic actually went to the brigade command on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe that we have other specific intercepts or documents which would indicate the physical presence of Major Obrenovic at the brigade command during the day of 14 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, this conversation, is there -- is this a normal -- is this relatively -- should you consider this normal for the duty officer to be taking part in this sort of exchange, or is this something out of the ordinary?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. If you refer back to the 1983 command and staff regulations, this type of a conversation is a classical function of the brigade or of any duty operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And let's go to the next exhibit. I believe as we're still on 14 July, you've chosen Exhibit 519.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. This is the regular or daily combat report, 14 July 1995, from the command of the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade to the command of the Drina Corps. It lays out in some detail the enemy situation as well as the primary tasks for the units. It notes that at the time of the writing of this report, one large column of Muslim extremists was routed at Velja Glava, and that is now returning towards Mladevac and Zljebac, while another went towards Bijela Zemlja. If I can move to the original B/C/S version of this document, it indicates the report going out at approximately 14 July, 1840 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do we get any indications from this document who may have drafted the report?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Going back to the English language translation, you see the initials DJ/MB. Given conversations that I've had with other VRS officers who perform the duty operations position, this indicates that the initials DJ are the person who actually drafted the report. And MB would be the individual who typed the report. Certainly within the context of all of the known events, this report in that situation would have been drafted by Major Jokic as the duty officer that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: To clarify something, you referred to your conversations with VRS people about -- are you talking about just the regular process of --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, just the regular process as not only my personal conversations, but interviews that were taken by investigators who were directed to ask these specific questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you're not making reference that somebody told you this was Dragan Jokic. You're just talking about the process by which these things are drafted?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So what do you base your opinion that this would have been Dragan Jokic on?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The initials DJ located here, coupled with the knowledge that on that day he was the duty operations officer. And further, in the absence of the commander or chief of staff, as a duty operations officer, it would have been his responsibility to draft the daily report for the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I really do not want to press the point, but it may be important in the future. DJ/MB are the initials that are in the translation, MB, rather. Since the document is originally in Cyrillic, the initials are actually MV. Could Mr. Butler please note that. This is for Misko V. Vasic, that is the person who created the document, and this is a person who will be of interest to the Defence in terms of authorship over the text. That is why I digressed and that is why I intervened. So the initials are not MB, as stated, but MV. Thank you. I beg your pardon once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, I think this issue that you could raise it during your cross-examination in the future. But this Trial Chamber would like to regard it as a matter of clarification. So, Mr. McCloskey, would you please ask some questions to this witness on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And thank you for clearing up the translation of Cyrillic. That's not always perfect, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, can you -- first of all, the second set of initials, did you learn who the -- not who by identity, but who by process that ought to be? What function does that person normally serve?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That second set of individuals is the assistant or clerk of the duty operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know anything about -- specifically about the person that Mr. Stojanovic mentioned?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't, in detail, have any knowledge of that individual. It's -- again, being handicapped by the ability to not read Cyrillic, I have to take it at face value with respect to the translation. But that is something that I could check on to verify.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 229, and it is an intercept from 14 July 1995 at 2038 hours. And just in highlighting the first line, there is a notation there that the frequency was not active from 1130 hours until 2020 hours that particular day, which was one of the first indications that I had that on that day that there may be communications difficulties with the overall communications network, which might preclude why in the greater context of intercepts we have very few intercepts, particularly with General Krstic or other players of the Drina Corps, during the greater part of that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you remind us also what was going on on the 14th in terms of military action towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to Zepa, by 1800 hours on 13 July, the command post of the -- or the forward command post had been activated, and the plan was that by the early morning hours on 14 July 1995, the VRS would kick off offensive activities against the Zepa enclave. It's my understanding that, in fact, did occur on time. So during the day of the 14th, those individuals at the IKM were dealing with the related issues of military operations towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Where do you think Krstic was on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that General Krstic on the 14th of July was at the IKM in Krivace.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So getting back to this exhibit, 229, it says that it's between General Zivanovic at Zlatar and Major Jokic, and it says in parentheses Palma duty officer. What do you take from this particular conversation?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the time by 2038 hours and placing this in context, not only through the day of the 13th, but when they could on the 14th, the Zvornik Brigade had been indicating to the command of the Drina Corps that they were being faced with an overwhelming number of Bosnian Muslim soldiers and individuals in the column who were rapidly moving into the deep part of the territory of the brigade. And as I indicated in my narrative with the surrounding contextual documents, that -- those initial reports were met with a certain degree of skepticism by the Drina Corps command, and if you go back to the last intercept exhibit, it even notes Zivanovic saying that the numbers -- the people are lying. By this time on the evening of 14 July 1995, certainly the scope of the size and the threat that this column presented to the Zvornik area was finally becoming clear even at the headquarters of the Drina Corps. And what you have here is a reflection of General Zivanovic who is still at the Drina Corps basically passing orders through the duty officer, Major Jokic, for Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I note in the third line Zivanovic says to Jokic, "Take this as an order." What do you make of that comment?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Presumably by then, everybody in the Drina Corps would have been aware that General Zivanovic was no longer the commander of the corps, given the fact that the order indicating that had gone out the night before. However, one of the normal principles of command and staff is that officers are only charged to give orders which they can do so under their competence or authority. So clearly in this instance, because of the events that were happening on the ground, General Zivanovic wanted to make it clear that he was issuing this as an order. The presumption behind it being that he had either discussed the issue with General Krstic or someone at the Main Staff - we don't know the answer to that and was passing an order due to the urgency of the situation and wanted to make it clear to the Palma duty officer that he was issuing this as an order and that it needed to be passed down to Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is there any of the information in this -- and I won't go over all the information with you, but the basic descriptions of the military information that appears to be falsified or absolutely incorrect to you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. And I just want to highlight the last line in this particular instance, and they are apparently still having some modulation problems with the communications gear. But within the larger context of the conversation, this appears to be a reflection of the Bosnian Muslim column's location and situation as the Zvornik Brigade and Drina Corps understood it at that time. And as we go to the Zvornik Brigade duty officer's logbook, we will see these same type of notations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, before we get there, let's go to the next exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, could we stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Oh, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, let's come to the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, I believe we're on Exhibit 232. And this is an intercept 14 July at 2102 hours. This is an intercept the Court, I believe, has seen a few times, so I just want to get your views on a couple of things. Let's go down to the middle of it after the mention of, "Is that Beara? Jokic here." Beara can't be heard. And Jokic says: "We were together, Colonel, sir, number 155 called you and asked you to call him urgently." Then it goes on to say: "That means the superior command." What do you think this number, 155, refers to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The phone number reference 155, as indicated in other intercept exhibits as well as a notation in the duty officer logbook reflects the phone number of General Miletic at a location called Panorama. Panorama is the telephonic code name for the headquarters of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Then, according to this, Jokic says: "Hey, we have huge problems over here." Then Beara can't be heard and Jokic says: "There are big problems. Well, with the people. I mean with the parcel." And then Beara can't be heard and Jokic says: "Who? And Drago is nowhere around. I don't know where the others are all day." What do you take, if anything, this reference to "big problems --" well, before we get to the problems, what do you take "the people, I mean the parcel," to be a reference to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular context, I believe that the people/parcel references that he's talking about are those Bosnian Muslim prisoners that are located at schools in the zone of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In context with the conversation first with Colonel Beara, I don't think that Colonel Beara is looking for information with respect to the numbers of individuals in the column. And second, when looking at the next sentence in context, "Drago is nowhere around." Drago, first name of Drago Nikolic, Lieutenant Drago Nikolic, the security officer of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. So I believe that the proper context of this conversation is, in fact, discussing the situation with prisoners in the schools in the zone of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us -- just remind us at 2102 hours on the 14th, what would that problem have been, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the things that when you look at the lash-up in context between the movement of the column into the zone of the Zvornik Brigade, and the issues pertaining to the guarding and execution of prisoners of war, is the fact that the Zvornik Brigade does not become significantly involved. The first major contact does not occur until approximately 2000 to 2100 hours on 13 July 1995 -- I'm sorry, 14 July 1995. If you refer back to the daily combat report which was published at 1800 hours that day, it does reflect the fact that the situation is normal. And while the brigade is anticipating significant contact, it has not yet occurred. In a subsequent exhibit, you will see the interim combat report, which discusses in detail that first contact. Now, at this point in time, the -- that first contact either has not yet occurred or is just occurring and that the duty officer at the Zvornik Brigade is not aware of all those details yet. And we will see that highlighted as this report comes into the duty officer in that future exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: In particular, and I know we've heard a lot of evidence on this, just outline briefly what the problem would be with the prisoners in your opinion at this time of night on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: By this time, 2100 hours on 14 July, according to our survivor accounts for Orahovac, the prisoners of war at that point have all been executed. However, there are such large numbers that the burial operations are continuing. Through the evening they'll suspend around midnight and start up the next morning. So while those executions are done, there are still hundreds of bodies on the surface. Our survivor accounts at Petkovci indicate some growing security problems of prisoners now being put in that location. They talk about in some detail about shootings and incidents that are happening in the school proper, indicating that there are concerns at least from the forces that are guarding these people about their ability to safely occur them. We see from our survivor accounts in the Pilica school a similar situation where the school is getting crowded to a point where the forces who are guarding the prisoners are no longer confident in their ability to be able to do that effectively. So I think in this context on the evening of 14 July is what Major Jokic is discussing with respect to the fact that they are having problems with the parcels. The sheer volume of prisoners that are coming in are overwhelming the ability of the Zvornik Brigade to secure them successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, let's go on to the next exhibit if we can. I believe it's 233.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you confirm the date of this intercept.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This intercept is 14 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, it says General Vilotic and Jokic duty officer from Palma. Again, I believe the Court has heard this, but are you aware of any General Vilotic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I am not. In researching this issue, certainly within the VRS there is no General Vilotic. And to the best of our ability to do so with the records that we have, we have even gone and looked for the name General Vilotic associated with the FRY army. And that name does not come up. But certainly in the context of the VRS, there is no General Vilotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So who do you think this is a reference to, if there is no General Vilotic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is a reference to General Miletic, who at this time is the chief of staff and acting -- or actually he is the chief of operations of the Main Staff and also performing duties as the acting chief of staff of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And let's just get into the intercept a little bit as we get to the bottom of the half page on the first page. It talks about the chief is still in the field -- sorry, the chief is in the field. And who would that be?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this respect, noticing your chief, as he says earlier Obrenovic, I take this to mean the chief of staff of the Zvornik Brigade, which would, at the time, be Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And then Jokic talks about problems at Perunik and then describes them. What in your view are the problems that Jokic is talking about at Perunik and is describing here. "But there's one big group. It's coming this way, towards -- well towards the asphalt, you know. I don't want to say it."

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this context, Major Jokic is informing General Miletic about the situation with respect to combat operations. Perunik is a terrain feature in the area of the Zvornik Brigade and he's also discussing the issue one group that they're surrounding, meaning elements of the column that they're attempting to surround.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So when Jokic says, "Well, we're trying to cut it off, but now we're having some problems. Some have been pushed back and now we're back, linking up, and so on." What do you think he means by that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he's discussing, again, the tactical military situation on the ground. His awareness that after the first contact, some of the column they perceive has been pushed back and that they're trying to now reestablish their own lines in order to continue ambush operations and attacking the head of the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Then on the top of the next page, "Well, that's it. And those ones promised me some reinforcements, but they still haven't arrived, you know." Jokic says this, according to this intercept. What do you make of that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We know from other documents and records, and particularly where we makes reference to the blue ones, that as the situation becomes more aware to everyone within the Drina Corps zone, that efforts are made to bring in, first, other police units from the special police brigade, and get them into the zone of the Zvornik Brigade in order to deal with combat operations. In fact, what happens in this case is those units do arrive, but they are held in the city of Zvornik. They don't report to the army, because of the dire threat that was perceived at the time that the city of Zvornik might actually be the object of attack by the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So in the section that you believe is Miletic, "Well, check with Vasic," expletive, "everything on two feet must be rounded up, has to be mobilised. Jokic sound the alert there in the town." Who do you think Vasic is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect I believe the individual in question is Dragomir Vasic, who is the head of CSB Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And there is more discussion about -- Miletic says, "Everybody who can carry a gun must go up there." And it goes on a bit. "Everyone must be mobilised." And Jokic says, "Understand, General, sir." Then we don't hear -- we can't understand something from Miletic. And Jokic says, "Obrenovic is really engaged to the maximum." What do you think he is referring to there, that one sentence?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That particular one sentence, I believe he is referring to the fact that at that time Major Obrenovic is completely engaged with dealing with issues with respect to the Bosnian Muslim column in his zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Then he says, "We all are, believe me." Then he says, "This packet has done most to ruin us ..." What can you make of that partial comment, "This packet has done most to ruin us"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this respect, I believe that what Major Obrenovic is referring to is the fact that he's now discussing that additional in-bound groups of prisoners --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let me just clarify. I know you've been on direct for too long, but who do you -- I think you said Major Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Major Jokic, my apologies. Major Jokic is indicating that the most recent batch of prisoners who had been sent in the zone of the Zvornik Brigade has now completely placed the brigade in a position where they are at the end of their limit to be able to successfully deal with that issue. And he indicates that since this morning we have been reporting on numbers of people, and it trails off.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What do you think he means when he says, "We've been reporting on the number of people"? What do you think that is a reference to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe in this particular context, he is discussing the number of prisoners that have been arriving in the zone of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And could he be speaking of the number of people in the column that have been approaching them that day as well?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a possibility, because we do have intercepts that indicate the numbers of people in the columns and that the Zvornik Brigade has, in fact, been discussing those with the Drina Corps. But for me, the fact that General Miletic doesn't want to discuss that indicates what I believe is my former interpretation. If he was interested as the chief of operations in dealing successfully with the column, he would want to know details about the size of the column and things of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And you're referring to the comment: "Okay, don't talk to me about that"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Then there's some more talk about Vasic. But I think that's enough for that exhibit. All right. The next exhibit is 520, I believe.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you tell us what this is.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the interim combat report dated 14 July 1995. And it reflects the events that occurred approximately 2020 hours. And this is the first significant combat activity that occurs in the zone of the Zvornik Brigade, which in fact results in a rupture of the lines of the -- between those units that were in ambush position. This is Major Obrenovic telling the command of the Drina Corps that it is realistic to expect a breakthrough in the area of responsibility of the 4th or 7th Battalion, either tonight or early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And again going down to the initials and based on what we've learned about Cyrillic recently, can you tell us what you think the initials are?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at the B/C/S version we have DJ and then the same initials MV.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So that B is a mistake like the last one?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And the MV, have you had a chance to look at any documents at your fingertips to help us with that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the July 1995 roster of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade command. This was a prior exhibit. I believe we discussed it on late Tuesday or early Wednesday. I don't have the exhibit number offhand at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's then just make reference to the ERN 008 -- 00846881, and we'll fix that with an exhibit number when Janet finds it.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the individual that we are discussing here is listed as number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And is this the document 520, going back to the interim. That last exhibit was 399, that roster of the brigade. This interim combat report, do we see information in this report written down anywhere else on another exhibit we're going to be getting to shortly?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. We'll see the same information as it is notated in the duty officer's logbook from the duty officer of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just for clarification, that what you're referring to has been referred to by people as the workbook, if we can try to -- and we'll get to that next, I believe.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So let's go to that workbook exhibit, if you've got it at your fingertips. I believe it's Exhibit 507. And that is the English version. And can you tell us where the OTP got this from and when you were able to really first look at this in any detail.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was provided by Colonel Dragan Obrenovic as a series of the documents that he provided to the Office of the Prosecutor. I've seen this document in the English language form for roughly about two months. I've seen the original document as well, accompanied with one of our translators. So one of the first things that I have been doing, in effect, while understanding the context of the document, is looking for instances in this particular workbook where I might be able to validate or at least cross-index notations and items with other pieces of information that I have. Clearly, from my own personal background perspective, I recognise that there is at least a potential for this document to have been fabricated. And certainly one of my concerns is in going through this document is to try to find as much other information that I can in order to try and confirm or deny that thesis. So a lot of my work, at least in the early part of that document, was done with respect to trying to determine whether or not we could back up or corroborate notations in this document with other documents within the context of the investigation and in my narrative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So at this stage of your review, have you had enough information to form an opinion yet, or is the -- is the jury still out in your mind on this document's authenticity?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an analyst, I never have enough information, but at this point I'm willing to say that the material that's in this log is consistent, not only with the number of specific documents which I'll discuss the Court, but also consistent in context with my broader understanding of the situation and occurrences that happened on the ground in the Zvornik Brigade during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But a really good forgery, you would expect that, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's go over some of the information in this. And let's start with the ERN of last three digits -- well, entire ERN 03089333, which I think, as we've learned, has been marked 13 July 1995 by Mr. Obrenovic in his analysis.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And could you just go through, commenting on anything in particular you think is relevant. We do not want to go through, obviously, all the detail in the entire book.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can direct the Court's attention to -- in the first instance page 3 of the English language translation, where I've highlighted a time notation of 1315 hours, and underneath it a notation of a bulldozer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What's the significance of that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that notation and the time is relatively consistent with the conversation that Colonel Milanovic had with the Palma duty officer that day looking for earth-moving equipment to have it sent to Konjevic Polje. So that is just one indicator that I used as something where I think there is a potential to corroborate that piece of information with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And just to be clear, you don't believe the duty officer on the 13th was Mr. Jokic, do you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know who the duty officer was on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe, and I would like to check my facts on this one, but I believe it was Captain Sreten Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What else do you want to talk about?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also on the 13th page 5. And while in the greater context of the discussion, this notation here pertaining to a phone call or contact from the president of the Zvornik municipality looking for a flatbed trailer to be sent to Bratunac to bring a bulldozer and then the notation 1000, Colonel Beara passed on the message. At this point in time, notwithstanding the association of Colonel Beara with this, I'm still unable to find any other information which would lend to corroborate that particular comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This reference to Colonel Beara, does this give us any indication where Colonel Beara might be if this is truly the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no indication on 13 July, just the notation that he passed the message. There is no notation whether it's his physical presence passing on the message or whether it's a telephonic conversation. So there's no way of knowing, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next section you wanted to note.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 7 of the English language translation --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And again we have a 14 July underlined, Jokic, which for the record was Mr. Obrenovic's stated. That was his reference.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular one, a fragment of a note on Colonel Salapura called. Drago and Beara are to report to Golic. The Court is aware of the identification of Drago and Beara. The individual Golic is Major Golic, an intelligence officer with the Drina Corps, and Colonel Salapura is an intelligence officer with the Main Staff intelligence directory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, Golic is a pretty common name in Bosnia, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So why do you think this Golic is the Drina Corps Golic that -- from the intel?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, given the fact that while it may be a relatively common name, within the context of the military hierarchy of the brigades in the corps, Major Golic is -- Major Pavle Golic is the only name of that last name that falls within the listing of those officers. And also the association of Drago and Beara as security officers, I believe it's a natural conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do we see Major Pavle Golic or do we see Major Golic's name come up in other documents related to the murder operation shortly after this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We will see Major Golic in a series of intercepts that occur on 16 July 1995 with respect to the executions at the Branjevo Military Farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Just to clarify the record on that, do these intercepts specifically refer to the executions at the farm and Mr. Golic, or are you referring to your interpretation of those intercepts?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. As we'll note in those intercepts, that series of intercepts refers to a series of conversations between the Palma duty officer and the duty officer at the Drina Corps as well as the security and rear services branches or the intelligence and rear services branch of the Drina Corps with respect to acquiring 500 litres of fuel for Colonel Popovic to finish his job.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So that -- we'll get to your interpretation on that. There's not a direct reference?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next section you wanted to point out.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the English language, page 9. A 1500 hour reference that Colonel Beara is coming and a fragmentary line, partially Orahovac, Petkovci, Rocevic, Pilica. And notwithstanding the first one, these are all known location sites where Bosnian Muslim men were being detained in the Zvornik Infantry Brigade area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, these various notes that you've referred to on the 14th, would this, in your view, be a normal part of the duty officer's job?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: These notes appear to be notations, which again are classical examples of the role and function of a duty officer. The conduit of information coming into the brigade and the notations - and again, I don't want to get into the context of the entire series - but notations of information coming into the brigade and the duty officer or the person writing this particular logbook, the notation, putting down what the significance of that information was and who it was passed to. So these are all consistent functions with that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. What else?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can go to page 13 of the English language of this one, I highlight this issue only in respect to the fact that I am aware of what Colonel Obrenovic has said about it, and I want to highlight that at this point in time I'm not in a position to be able to confirm or deny his particular interpretation. It would take some more research and going through records to be able to lend my credence to that. So I just wanted to highlight that, the fact that I'm not in a position to confirm or deny that at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you just tell us what this -- what the potential options for the meaning of this is, in your opinion.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are -- because there are so many -- I mean, first Pelemis is a location, a series of villages. Pelemis is also the last name of a number of people, both inside the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, as well as outside. Certainly the Court is aware of the identification of Milorad Pelemis of the 10th Sabotage Detachment. But there are a number of other individuals with that last name in the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. I believe Colonel Obrenovic has indicated that his belief is that the individual in question here is an individual functioning as either the deputy or acting commander of the 1st Infantry Battalion. And his interpretation of having problems with personnel may be related to issues at Pilica. It may also be in respect to issues with elements or reports that members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment may have committed executions at Petkovci school. Given the fact that there are so many interpretations, that's why I'm highlighting the fact that at the present point in time, I'm not able to confirm or deny any of these interpretations. We're still doing the research on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 14, there is a notation highlighted Jokic and a delegation from Pilica. In this particular respect, I understand it is a course of interviews conducted by the investigation team.
