Again, as I've discussed, this is a document where after this commission has come through, Colonel Pandurevic in a rather lengthy series of paragraphs outlines the entire historical context of not only this battle, but previous battles that have been engaged in by elements of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, making the point to the Drina Corps command that over the past six months, Colonel Pandurevic feels that his brigade has borne an inordinate share or brunt of the war. Of note, at least with respect to the criminal aspects, is his discussion of the situation of the territory in paragraph 4, which is page 2 of the English language translation, where he notes the situation, not only where they swamped, but that: It is inconceivable to me, personally Colonel Pandurevic, that someone brought in 3.000 Turks of military age and placed them in schools in the municipality, in addition to the 7.000 or so who fled in the forest. You notice that this created an extremely complex situation and the possibility of total occupation of Zvornik, in conjunction with the forces at the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have anything else you want to say on that particular document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at the B/C/S version of that, again the signature which I attribute to Colonel Vinko Pandurevic, indicating his personal and direct knowledge of these issues. Again, on the broader sense of this, it lets the -- it lays the indication that while Colonel Pandurevic was aware of the decision to move these prisoners into his brigade zone, it lays the inference that Colonel Pandurevic himself did not make that decision. And now in retrospect, the fact that it appeared to be an extremely poor decision at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Does this document give us any idea of precisely when Vinko Pandurevic would have been aware of the operation to capture, detain, transport, and kill the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't believe it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've probably got about 10 or 15 minutes, which we're ready either Monday or now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe we could sit 10 minutes more and finish your direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Butler, could we go to the next exhibit, 541.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Moving forward in time now to September 1995, this is a document that was, of course, seized out of the headquarters of the Zvornik Brigade by the OTP. And what this document reflects is that there has been approval of 5 tons of diesel fuel for carrying out engineer works in the zone of responsibility of the Drina Corps and that it will be delivered. Of interest in this particular case is the fact that the fuel is being directed to be delivered to Captain Milorad Trpic, whom I believe is, in fact, Captain Milorad Trbic, and that there's a misspelling in the context of the message. Captain Trbic, of course, is a security officer with the Zvornik Infantry Brigade, and that he is the one who is going to be designated to be responsible for the accurate maintenance of records and engine hours worked during this engineering project.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And do you have another exhibit on that same topic, Exhibit 542?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular one, also dated 14 September, showing the normal flow of orders from the commander of the Main Staff to the technical services people to issue the fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what do you think this fuel was used for?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly the pact to putting an engineer -- security officer in charge of accounting for engine vehicles and hours is unusual. We have the engineer equipment and vehicle logs for September and October 1995 from the Zvornik Brigade, and unlike the ones in July, activity related to these types of engineering processes is not listed in those logs. It is my understanding, not only based on the documents but also based on the continuing investigation, that this fuel was, in fact, used to accomplish what we call the reburial process or the process of exhuming the mass -- the mass graves, the primary sites, and distributing them to only 20 secondary sites in and around the zone of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Butler, now let's briefly, to finish up, go back to the workbook of the Zvornik Brigade, I believe where you -- if we could go where you left off.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 18 of that document, I have highlighted a reference to the notation of death of an individual. If you refer back to the 14 July 1995 report, the daily combat report of the Bratunac Brigade, it will reflect the name of this individual as a member of the 4th Battalion being killed. As I've noted in my previous testimony, the 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade was also, in fact, the 8th Battalion of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. And as much, as a matter of course, the death of this soldier from Bratunac, even though it originated -- from -- since his brigade did originate from Zvornik is being listed as a matter in the duty officer logbook. Just another piece to help confirm some of the validity of the issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know what date this man was killed?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I believe it's 15 July 1995, not 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And just in continuing your practice of identifying some of the information, can you tell us where -- what page to go to.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 19 of the English language translation, where on 15 July and a notation, Badem dispatched reinforcements. And this is at roughly 9.21 in the morning on 15 July 1995. Now, in this particular instance, we kind of come back to being at odds with the intercept that was discussed in detail, the reinforcements from Badem don't arrive until almost 2100 hours that night. So there really is a question as to just what these dispatched reinforcements means.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The people that arrived at 2100 hours arrived on --

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We're on 15 July. Let me retract that. In this context it's the individuals who are noted as arriving on 15 July in the daily combat report. I got my dates mixed up. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's continue to -- what's the next comment you wanted to make?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Coupled with that, 15 July reflecting the fact that the men from Bratunac had arrived at Parlog.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What page is that?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 22 of the English language translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 23 of the English language translation, there is a notation that somebody or something should communicate to Popovic that his proposal has been approved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know what that is?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. What's the next entry?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 24 of the English language translation, just following that, a notation that Drago and Lieutenant Colonel Popovic are to report to Major Golic early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know what that's a reference to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may, in fact, be a reference to them wanting to check in on the morning of 16 July as for what the situation is. But I don't want to take it any further beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know who Drago might be?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this context, I believe Drago is Drago Nikolic, the security officer of the Drina Corps -- I'm sorry, the Zvornik Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Further down on page 24, there's a request from the 1st Infantry Battalion for 50 litres of oil, 20 litres of gasoline, 10 crates of 7.62 millimetre ammunition, and a line designated for transport of troops to Kula. In the 1st Battalion sector, Kula is the school at Pilica where Bosnian Muslim men were known to be held on 15 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. What's next? And on page 25 we come to Mr. Obrenovic's 16 July designation.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. And again, just to highlight, and I won't put it up on the ELMO, the notation about the individual who died at the hospital. And then on 26 of the English language translation, now on 16 July, 0855, Golic asked Popovic to call him, indicating that you can forget what you asked for. Apparently there was a change in plans. What he wrote about, indicating that whatever that proposal was, it was something that was passed in writing. He knows what he's supposed to do, agreed with the procedure from the boss at panorama 01. In this context, the boss from panorama 01 should be General Mladic. Panorama, being the telephonic code name of the Main Staff. 01 is a suffix we frequently see associated with the commander, and it notes that this message was convoyed to Popovic at 0910 hours. There is another notation at the bottom of this page, reflecting that Beara is to call Panorama 155 at 0930. On page 27 of the English language translation, a reflection of notice that on the 16th of July 1995, at 1050 hours, 35 soldiers from the East Bosnia Corps were sent to the IKM. These soldiers are military police from the East Bosnia Corps and are, in fact, noted on the 16 July interim combat report as one of the few forces of reinforcements that did, in fact, arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The Panteri unit from the East Bosnia Corps are not a military police unit, are they?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, they are not to my knowledge. It also notes receiving that 1115 hours on 16 July it was reported from Zlatar that a triage of wounded and prisoners must to be carried out and this was reported to Beara. We see that in context with a previous intercept exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what specific reference are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, say again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What specific word are you referencing to another intercept?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The context of triage of wounded and prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that an intercept on what date?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the morning of 16 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. What else?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And further it notes that 1100 -- at 1120 hours on 16 July, conversation from Badem, Colonel Jankovic called and was looking for Major Malinic, and that that message was conveyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, we know Badem and we know Colonel Jankovic. Can you remind us who Major Malinic may be?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Malinic in this context is the commander of the Military Police Battalion of the 65th Protection Regiment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you have any documents or intercepts that indicate he's up in the Zvornik area, aside from this?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. On page 28 on 16 -- I'm sorry, on 16 July, another report from Zlatar that, "Our parcel is on its way. 30 will arrive in one hour and another parcel is expected at around 1600 hours." In this context, I believe what they're doing is they're now tracking the reinforcements that are now arriving in the zone. I don't believe that these parcels, in fact, refer to prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. What's the next point?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD JOHN BUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 29, the notation that at 1400 hours Popovic requested a bus with a full tank and 500 litres of D2. The Zlatar duty officer and Golic informed. And that, of course, corresponds to a previous intercept exhibit. On page 30 of the English language translation, and as we've discussed in some detail before, starting in the late afternoon hours, a series of messages from Zlatar that somebody is to go immediately to the commander, send a written report on the current situation. And in this context, the first individual is Mijatovic who is an operations officer at the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. This follows that now Colonel Popovic is directed to go find Vinko in the field. And that he must report back to the duty officer -- or that he should come back from the 1st Battalion area where he is so that he can be sent on a task by Zlatar. And again, as a point of reference Pilica and the Branjevo Military Farm are located in the zone of the 1st Battalion of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. At 1705, it reflects 30 soldiers arriving from Vlasenica. Again, this corresponds roughly to the intercept. Zlatar is again asking whether they had a report from the commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, I'm sorry. I understand that, but we have been told that at 2.15, there is another function will be happening in this courtroom. We have to leave this courtroom on time, so maybe next Monday you could continue the direct examination and I would like to thank the interpreters, the typists, as well as the technicians for their cooperation. And we'll resume at 9.00 Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
